entry.title: Taxpayers won't be penalised for inaccurate intermediary-submitted income details
entry.summary: Taxpayers won’t be penalised because of inaccurate details submitted by intermediaries IRAS · Oct 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore says taxpayers will not be penalised if tax assessments must be revised because intermediaries submitted incomplete or inaccurate income information, as intermediaries are responsible for its accuracy. In the Grab case, Grab submitted corrected income records, and IRAS will revise the assessments of affected private-hire car drivers and issue revised tax bills.

entry.title: New digital tools from IRAS to simplify 2026 corporate income tax filing
entry.summary: Tax Made Simple; Business Made Stronger: New Digital Resources to Ease Corporate Income Tax Filing in 2026 IRAS · Oct 19, 2026 · GuidanceThe Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has expanded its digital self-help resources for corporate income tax (CIT) filing for YA 2026, covering over 323,000 companies. The announcement describes tools available before, during and after filing, along with related tax support measures. It also outlines enforcement action and penalties against companies that fail to file on time.

entry.title: IRAS Warns Against False or Unsupported Employment Expense Claims
entry.summary: IRAS Warns Against False, Incorrect or Unsupported Employment Expense Claims IRAS · Oct 21, 2026 · GuidanceThe Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has found misleading online information urging taxpayers to claim employment expenses that were not incurred or are not tax deductible. Taxpayers are advised not to rely on such information and to ensure their claims are accurate and supported by records. Incorrect claims should be amended or withdrawn immediately through the 'Amend Tax Bill' service.
